children: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (NSE:HAL) reported Q2 FY27 revenue up 14.9% year over year to ₹7,613 crore and profit up 16% to ₹1,936 crore, while EBITDA margin fell to 22.8%. Management guided for FY27 revenue growth of 10–12% and an EBITDA margin of 30–31%.
Previous Week Recap
Q2 Revenue And Profit Growth
: HAL’s Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.9% year over year to ₹7,613 crore, while profit grew 16% to ₹1,936 crore. EBITDA increased 11.6% to ₹1,738 crore; margin fell to 22.8%.
Tejas Mk1A Delivery Target
: HAL received 14 GE F404 engines by October 2026 and built about 27 LCA Mk1A airframes, pending final tests. It targets delivery of around 10 aircraft to the Indian Air Force by March 2027.
FY27 Growth And Margin Guidance
: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) management guided for FY27 revenue growth of 10–12% and an EBITDA margin of 30–31%.
Engine Deliveries And Order Book
: HAL received 14 GE engines for Tejas Mk1A. Motilal Oswal expects deliveries to start in 4QFY27 and project execution to rise, citing an implied order book of INR 2.4 trillion.
Inventory Rise, Delivery Outlook
: HAL’s inventory rose about 28% in the first half of FY27, possibly as LCA Mk1A production outpaced deliveries. HSBC expects deliveries by FY27-end; CLSA sees them starting in H2.
HATSOFF Becomes Wholly Owned
: - Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)’s board approved the acquisition of the remaining 50% stake in HATSOFF Helicopter Technologies, making the joint venture a wholly owned subsidiary.
Citi Maintains Buy Rating
: Citi kept its Buy rating and Rs.6,175 target for HAL. Q2 revenue met estimates, but EBITDA missed on weaker margins. Engines, helicopters and repairs offset delays in Tejas Mk1A deliveries.
Inventory Signals Order Readiness
: HAL inventory rose 39% year over year, which Citi said signals greater order readiness as the company works to resolve Tejas Mk1A delivery bottlenecks.
Safran Helicopter Engine Joint Venture
: HAL and Safran finalized a SAFHAL joint venture deal to develop the 3,500–4,000 shp Aravalli helicopter engine for India’s IMRH and naval variant.
Motilal Oswal Raises Target
: - Motilal Oswal maintained its estimates and reiterated a BUY rating on Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), raising its target price to INR 5,900 from INR 5,800.
